title: Vanishing for the homology sheaf of a complex of quasi-coherent modules on the etale and fppf sites
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project — More on Cohomology of Spaces

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-vanishing-adequate at source lines 1615-1639: for a complex F_1 -> F_2 -> F_3 of quasi-coherent O_X-modules, the homology sheaf H_etale on the big etale site (built from the pi_X^*-pullbacks) equals epsilon_{X,*}H_fppf for the corresponding fppf homology sheaf, and both H^p_etale(U, H_etale) and H^p_fppf(U, H_fppf) vanish for p > 0 at every affine object U. The author's proof at source lines 1649-1703 first studies the restriction of H_etale to U_etale, identifies it with the degree-one homology of the complex f^*F_bullet using i_f o pi_X = f, observes that it is quasi-coherent, and shows compatibility with flat base change g : V -> U; then deduces the fppf sheaf property for H_etale from part (1) of the chapter's quasi-coherent review lemma (retained as context), which identifies H_fppf with H_etale; and finally proves the vanishing by applying the Cech vanishing criterion for the collection of affine objects with finite fppf coverings (a cross-chapter pointer), rewriting the Cech complex using the first paragraph, and concluding by Cech vanishing for quasi-coherent modules on a standard covering (a second pointer). The counted argument is therefore a complete three-part proof whose in-chapter ingredient is available inside the package.
